ko.explanation: 누군가나 무언가에 대한 깊은 애정. 연인 간의 사랑, 가족 간의 사랑, 취미나 활동에 대한 사랑 등 다양하게 쓰인다.

examples.advanced: 사랑은 누구나 경험하는 자연스러운 감정입니다.
examples.master: 사랑이라는 감정의 뉘앙스를 이해하면 한국어 의사소통이 깊어집니다.

en.explanation: A deep affection for someone or something. Used for romantic love, family love, and love for things/activities.

examples.intermediate: Today was a day full of love.
examples.advanced: Love is a natural emotion that everyone experiences.
examples.master: Understanding the nuance of "love" deepens Korean communication.

formal: My love and respect for you is eternal.
You have all my love and devotion.
casual: You mean so much to me!

ko.explanation: 행복하거나 만족스러운 상태. 명사 '행복' 또는 형용사 '행복하다'로 사용할 수 있다.

examples.advanced: 행복은 누구나 경험하는 자연스러운 감정입니다.
examples.master: 행복이라는 감정의 뉘앙스를 이해하면 한국어 의사소통이 깊어집니다.

en.explanation: A state of being happy or content. Can be used as noun '행복' or adjective '행복하다' (to be happy).

examples.intermediate: Today was a day full of happiness.
examples.advanced: Happiness is a natural emotion that everyone experiences.
examples.master: Understanding the nuance of "happiness" deepens Korean communication.

formal: May happiness be with you always.
Wishing you all the best and happiness.

ko.explanation: 슬프거나 불행한 감정. 형용사형은 '슬프다'이다.

examples.advanced: 슬픔은 누구나 경험하는 자연스러운 감정입니다.
examples.master: 슬픔이라는 감정의 뉘앙스를 이해하면 한국어 의사소통이 깊어집니다.

en.explanation: A feeling of sorrow or unhappiness. The adjective form is '슬프다' (to be sad).

examples.intermediate: Today was a day full of sadness.
examples.advanced: Sadness is a natural emotion that everyone experiences.
examples.master: Understanding the nuance of "sadness" deepens Korean communication.

ko.explanation: 그때그때 느끼는 마음의 상태. '기분이 좋다/나쁘다'로 자주 사용된다.

examples.advanced: 기분은 누구나 경험하는 자연스러운 감정입니다.
examples.master: 기분이라는 감정의 뉘앙스를 이해하면 한국어 의사소통이 깊어집니다.

en.explanation: The emotional state one feels at a given moment. Often used as '기분이 좋다/나쁘다' (to feel good/bad).

examples.intermediate: Today was a day full of mood / feeling.
examples.advanced: Mood / Feeling is a natural emotion that everyone experiences.
examples.master: Understanding the nuance of "mood / feeling" deepens Korean communication.

ko.explanation: 앞으로 일어날 일에 대해 불안해하는 마음. '걱정하다', '걱정되다'로 동사화된다.

examples.advanced: 걱정은 누구나 경험하는 자연스러운 감정입니다.
examples.master: 걱정이라는 감정의 뉘앙스를 이해하면 한국어 의사소통이 깊어집니다.

en.explanation: Anxiety about future events. Used as verbs '걱정하다' (to worry) and '걱정되다' (to be worried about).

examples.intermediate: Today was a day full of worry / concern.
examples.advanced: Worry / Concern is a natural emotion that everyone experiences.
examples.master: Understanding the nuance of "worry / concern" deepens Korean communication.

ko.explanation: 분노의 감정이 생기다. '화가 나다'의 줄임말로도 쓰인다. 명사형은 '화'이다.

examples.advanced: 화나는 것은 생활에서 중요한 부분입니다.
examples.master: 화나고 나면 늘 보람을 느낍니다.

en.explanation: To become angry or upset. Also used as '화가 나다'. The noun form is '화' (anger).

examples.intermediate: These days I often get angry.
examples.advanced: It is important to get angry regularly in life.
examples.master: After you get angry, you always feel a sense of accomplishment.

ko.explanation: 두려움을 느끼다. 공포 영화, 어두운 곳, 위험한 상황 등에서 느끼는 감정을 표현한다.

examples.advanced: 무섭다고 느끼는 것은 사람마다 다릅니다.
examples.master: "무섭다"의 정도를 다양하게 표현할 수 있으면 한국어가 풍부해집니다.

en.explanation: To feel fear. Used to express feelings about horror movies, dark places, dangerous situations, etc.

examples.beginner: This is really scary / to be scared!
examples.intermediate: It's not as scary / to be scared as I thought.
examples.advanced: Feeling that something is scary / to be scared varies from person to person.
examples.master: Being able to express varying degrees of "scary / to be scared" enriches your Korean.

ko.explanation: 불쾌하거나 귀찮은 감정이 생기다. 일상에서 자주 쓰이는 표현이다.

examples.advanced: 짜증나는 것은 생활에서 중요한 부분입니다.
examples.master: 짜증나고 나면 늘 보람을 느낍니다.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.translation: I went to be annoyed / frustrated.

en.explanation: To feel annoyed or irritated. A very commonly used expression in daily life.

examples.beginner: I want to be annoyed / frustrated.
examples.intermediate: These days I often be annoyed / frustrated.
examples.advanced: It is important to be annoyed / frustrated regularly in life.
examples.master: After you be annoyed / frustrated, you always feel a sense of accomplishment.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: I went to be annoyed / frustrated.

ko.explanation: 할 일이 없어서 지루하다. 재미있는 일이 없을 때 느끼는 감정을 표현한다.

examples.advanced: 심심하다고 느끼는 것은 사람마다 다릅니다.
examples.master: "심심하다"의 정도를 다양하게 표현할 수 있으면 한국어가 풍부해집니다.

en.explanation: To feel bored due to having nothing to do. Expresses the feeling when there's nothing interesting happening.

examples.intermediate: It's not as bored as I thought.
examples.advanced: Feeling that something is bored varies from person to person.
examples.master: Being able to express varying degrees of "bored" enriches your Korean.

ko.explanation: 기대감이나 흥분으로 마음이 두근거리다. 주로 연애, 새로운 시작, 기대되는 일에 사용한다.

examples.advanced: 설레는 것은 생활에서 중요한 부분입니다.
examples.master: 설레고 나면 늘 보람을 느낍니다.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.translation: I went to be excited / flutter (heart).

en.explanation: To have one's heart flutter with anticipation or excitement. Often used for romance, new beginnings, or exciting events.

examples.beginner: I want to be excited / flutter (heart).
examples.intermediate: These days I often be excited / flutter (heart).
examples.advanced: It is important to be excited / flutter (heart) regularly in life.
examples.master: After you be excited / flutter (heart), you always feel a sense of accomplishment.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: I went to be excited / flutter (heart).

ko.explanation: 좋은 일이 있어서 마음이 즐겁다. 행복과 비슷하지만 더 순간적인 감정.

examples.advanced: 기쁘다고 느끼는 것은 사람마다 다릅니다.
examples.master: "기쁘다"의 정도를 다양하게 표현할 수 있으면 한국어가 풍부해집니다.

en.explanation: To feel glad because of something good. Similar to happiness but more momentary.

examples.intermediate: It's not as glad / joyful as I thought.
examples.advanced: Feeling that something is glad / joyful varies from person to person.
examples.master: Being able to express varying degrees of "glad / joyful" enriches your Korean.

ko.explanation: 혼자여서 쓸쓸하고 마음이 허전하다.

examples.advanced: 외롭다고 느끼는 것은 사람마다 다릅니다.
examples.master: "외롭다"의 정도를 다양하게 표현할 수 있으면 한국어가 풍부해집니다.

en.explanation: Feeling lonely and empty because of being alone.

examples.intermediate: It's not as lonely as I thought.
examples.advanced: Feeling that something is lonely varies from person to person.
examples.master: Being able to express varying degrees of "lonely" enriches your Korean.

ko.explanation: 창피하거나 쑥스러운 감정. 실수를 했거나 칭찬을 받을 때 느낀다.

examples.advanced: 부끄럽다고 느끼는 것은 사람마다 다릅니다.
examples.master: "부끄럽다"의 정도를 다양하게 표현할 수 있으면 한국어가 풍부해집니다.

en.explanation: Feeling embarrassed or shy. Felt when making mistakes or receiving compliments.

examples.intermediate: It's not as embarrassed / shy as I thought.
examples.advanced: Feeling that something is embarrassed / shy varies from person to person.
examples.master: Being able to express varying degrees of "embarrassed / shy" enriches your Korean.

ko.explanation: 감사하는 마음을 나타내는 말. '감사하다'보다 친근한 느낌.

examples.advanced: 고맙다고 느끼는 것은 사람마다 다릅니다.
examples.master: "고맙다"의 정도를 다양하게 표현할 수 있으면 한국어가 풍부해집니다.

en.explanation: Expressing gratitude. More casual than '감사하다'.

examples.intermediate: It's not as thankful / grateful as I thought.
examples.advanced: Feeling that something is thankful / grateful varies from person to person.
examples.master: Being able to express varying degrees of "thankful / grateful" enriches your Korean.

ko.explanation: 반복되어 싫증이 나다. 지루함보다 더 강한 표현.

examples.advanced: 지겹다고 느끼는 것은 사람마다 다릅니다.
examples.master: "지겹다"의 정도를 다양하게 표현할 수 있으면 한국어가 풍부해집니다.

en.explanation: Fed up from repetition. Stronger than being bored.

examples.beginner: This is really sick of / tired of!
examples.intermediate: It's not as sick of / tired of as I thought.
examples.advanced: Feeling that something is sick of / tired of varies from person to person.
examples.master: Being able to express varying degrees of "sick of / tired of" enriches your Korean.

ko.explanation: 이전에 한 일에 대해 잘못했다고 느끼는 마음.

examples.advanced: 후회는 누구나 경험하는 자연스러운 감정입니다.
examples.master: 후회이라는 감정의 뉘앙스를 이해하면 한국어 의사소통이 깊어집니다.

en.explanation: Feeling sorry for something done in the past.

examples.intermediate: Today was a day full of regret.
examples.advanced: Regret is a natural emotion that everyone experiences.
examples.master: Understanding the nuance of "regret" deepens Korean communication.

ko.explanation: 속이 막힌 것처럼 갑갑하고 불편하다. 물리적, 정서적 상황 모두에 사용.

examples.advanced: 답답하다고 느끼는 것은 사람마다 다릅니다.
examples.master: "답답하다"의 정도를 다양하게 표현할 수 있으면 한국어가 풍부해집니다.

en.explanation: Feeling suffocated or frustrated. Used for both physical and emotional situations.

examples.intermediate: It's not as frustrated / stuffy as I thought.
examples.advanced: Feeling that something is frustrated / stuffy varies from person to person.
examples.master: Being able to express varying degrees of "frustrated / stuffy" enriches your Korean.

ko.explanation: 짐이 없는 것처럼 마음이 가볍고 후련하다.

examples.advanced: 홀가분하다고 느끼는 것은 사람마다 다릅니다.
examples.master: "홀가분하다"의 정도를 다양하게 표현할 수 있으면 한국어가 풍부해집니다.

en.explanation: Feeling light and relieved as if a burden is lifted.

examples.intermediate: It's not as light-hearted / relieved as I thought.
examples.advanced: Feeling that something is light-hearted / relieved varies from person to person.
examples.master: Being able to express varying degrees of "light-hearted / relieved" enriches your Korean.

ko.explanation: 마음이 편하지 않고 초조하다. 걱정과 비슷하지만 더 급한 느낌.

examples.advanced: 불안하다고 느끼는 것은 사람마다 다릅니다.
examples.master: "불안하다"의 정도를 다양하게 표현할 수 있으면 한국어가 풍부해집니다.

en.explanation: Feeling restless and nervous. Similar to worry but more urgent.

examples.intermediate: It's not as anxious / uneasy as I thought.
examples.advanced: Feeling that something is anxious / uneasy varies from person to person.
examples.master: Being able to express varying degrees of "anxious / uneasy" enriches your Korean.

ko.explanation: 어이없고 말도 안 되는 상황에서 느끼는 감정.

examples.advanced: 황당하다고 느끼는 것은 사람마다 다릅니다.
examples.master: "황당하다"의 정도를 다양하게 표현할 수 있으면 한국어가 풍부해집니다.

en.explanation: Feeling when facing a ridiculous or unbelievable situation.

examples.intermediate: It's not as absurd / dumbfounded as I thought.
examples.advanced: Feeling that something is absurd / dumbfounded varies from person to person.
examples.master: Being able to express varying degrees of "absurd / dumbfounded" enriches your Korean.

ko.explanation: 기분이 가라앉고 슬픈 상태가 계속되다.

examples.advanced: 우울하다고 느끼는 것은 사람마다 다릅니다.
examples.master: "우울하다"의 정도를 다양하게 표현할 수 있으면 한국어가 풍부해집니다.

en.explanation: A continuous state of feeling down and sad.

examples.intermediate: It's not as depressed / blue as I thought.
examples.advanced: Feeling that something is depressed / blue varies from person to person.
examples.master: Being able to express varying degrees of "depressed / blue" enriches your Korean.

ko.explanation: 다른 사람이 가진 것을 부러워하며 미워하는 마음.

examples.advanced: 질투는 누구나 경험하는 자연스러운 감정입니다.
examples.master: 질투이라는 감정의 뉘앙스를 이해하면 한국어 의사소통이 깊어집니다.

en.explanation: Envying and resenting what others have.

examples.intermediate: Today was a day full of jealousy.
examples.advanced: Jealousy is a natural emotion that everyone experiences.
examples.master: Understanding the nuance of "jealousy" deepens Korean communication.

ko.explanation: 답답하던 것이 해결되어 마음이 시원하다.

examples.advanced: 후련하다고 느끼는 것은 사람마다 다릅니다.
examples.master: "후련하다"의 정도를 다양하게 표현할 수 있으면 한국어가 풍부해집니다.

en.explanation: Feeling refreshed after something frustrating is resolved.

examples.intermediate: It's not as relieved / refreshed as I thought.
examples.advanced: Feeling that something is relieved / refreshed varies from person to person.
examples.master: Being able to express varying degrees of "relieved / refreshed" enriches your Korean.

ko.explanation: 감정이나 욕구를 억누르다. 화, 눈물, 웃음 등을 참을 때 사용.

examples.advanced: 참는 것은 생활에서 중요한 부분입니다.
examples.master: 참고 나면 늘 보람을 느낍니다.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.translation: I went to endure / hold back.

en.explanation: To suppress emotions or desires. Used for holding back anger, tears, laughter, etc.

examples.beginner: I want to endure / hold back.
examples.intermediate: These days I often endure / hold back.
examples.advanced: It is important to endure / hold back regularly in life.
examples.master: After you endure / hold back, you always feel a sense of accomplishment.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: I went to endure / hold back.

ko.explanation: 사람의 마음속에 일어나는 여러 가지 감정의 총체.

examples.advanced: 정서는 누구나 경험하는 자연스러운 감정입니다.
examples.master: 정서이라는 감정의 뉘앙스를 이해하면 한국어 의사소통이 깊어집니다.

en.explanation: The totality of various feelings in one's mind.

examples.intermediate: Today was a day full of emotions / sentiments.
examples.advanced: Emotions / Sentiments is a natural emotion that everyone experiences.
examples.master: Understanding the nuance of "emotions / sentiments" deepens Korean communication.

ko.explanation: 기쁨, 슬픔, 분노 등 마음의 느낌. 정서보다 더 일반적인 표현.

examples.advanced: 감정은 누구나 경험하는 자연스러운 감정입니다.
examples.master: 감정이라는 감정의 뉘앙스를 이해하면 한국어 의사소통이 깊어집니다.

en.explanation: Feelings of the heart like joy, sadness, anger. More general than 'jeongseo'.

examples.intermediate: Today was a day full of emotion / feeling.
examples.advanced: Emotion / Feeling is a natural emotion that everyone experiences.
examples.master: Understanding the nuance of "emotion / feeling" deepens Korean communication.

ko.explanation: 기운이 빠지고 의기소침해지다. 자신감이 떨어질 때 사용.

examples.advanced: 기죽는 것은 생활에서 중요한 부분입니다.
examples.master: 기죽고 나면 늘 보람을 느낍니다.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.translation: I went to be dispirited / disheartened.

en.explanation: To lose energy and become dejected. Used when confidence drops.

examples.beginner: I want to be dispirited / disheartened.
examples.intermediate: These days I often be dispirited / disheartened.
examples.advanced: It is important to be dispirited / disheartened regularly in life.
examples.master: After you be dispirited / disheartened, you always feel a sense of accomplishment.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: I went to be dispirited / disheartened.

ko.explanation: 기분이 들떠서 즐겁고 흥이 나다.

examples.advanced: 신나는 것은 생활에서 중요한 부분입니다.
examples.master: 신나고 나면 늘 보람을 느낍니다.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.translation: I went to excited / pumped up.

en.explanation: Feeling elated, happy, and energetic.

examples.intermediate: These days I often excited / pumped up.
examples.advanced: It is important excited / pumped up regularly in life.
examples.master: After you excited / pumped up, you always feel a sense of accomplishment.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: I went to excited / pumped up.

ko.explanation: 마음에 들어 흡족하다. 기대에 부합할 때 느끼는 감정.

examples.advanced: 만족하는 것은 생활에서 중요한 부분입니다.
examples.master: 만족하고 나면 늘 보람을 느낍니다.

en.explanation: Feeling pleased and content. Felt when expectations are met.

examples.advanced: It is important satisfied regularly in life.
examples.master: After you satisfied, you always feel a sense of accomplishment.

ko.explanation: 기대했던 것이 이루어지지 않아 낙심하다.

examples.advanced: 실망하는 것은 생활에서 중요한 부분입니다.
examples.master: 실망하고 나면 늘 보람을 느낍니다.

en.explanation: Feeling let down when expectations aren't met.

examples.advanced: It is important disappointed regularly in life.
examples.master: After you disappointed, you always feel a sense of accomplishment.

ko.explanation: 깊이 마음이 움직이다. 영화, 음악, 다른 사람의 행동에서 느끼는 감정.

examples.advanced: 감동하는 것은 생활에서 중요한 부분입니다.
examples.master: 감동하고 나면 늘 보람을 느낍니다.

en.explanation: Deeply moved emotionally. Felt from movies, music, or others' actions.

examples.intermediate: These days I often moved / touched.
examples.advanced: It is important moved / touched regularly in life.
examples.master: After you moved / touched, you always feel a sense of accomplishment.

ko.explanation: 마음이 아프고 괴롭다. 서운함과 슬픔이 섞인 감정.

examples.advanced: 속상하다고 느끼는 것은 사람마다 다릅니다.
examples.master: "속상하다"의 정도를 다양하게 표현할 수 있으면 한국어가 풍부해집니다.

en.explanation: Feeling hurt and distressed. A mix of disappointment and sadness.

examples.intermediate: It's not as upset / hurt as I thought.
examples.advanced: Feeling that something is upset / hurt varies from person to person.
examples.master: Being able to express varying degrees of "upset / hurt" enriches your Korean.

ko.explanation: 좋은 결과나 일이 일어나기를 바라다.

examples.advanced: 기대하는 것은 생활에서 중요한 부분입니다.
examples.master: 기대하고 나면 늘 보람을 느낍니다.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.translation: I went to expect / look forward to.

en.explanation: To hope for good results or things to happen.

examples.beginner: I want to expect / look forward to.
examples.intermediate: These days I often expect / look forward to.
examples.advanced: It is important to expect / look forward to regularly in life.
examples.master: After you expect / look forward to, you always feel a sense of accomplishment.
